title: The Green Mile
synopsis: A death row in 1935, a giant inmate who heals what he touches, and a guard who has to decide what mercy means in a green corridor.

nodes.text: A mouse on the green linoleum that everyone pretends not to see. The moment in Mr. New Inmate will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Leave a crumb” than after “Set the trap.”

choices.consequence: You commit to leave a crumb. By New Inmate, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You choose to set the trap. It opens the route to New Inmate, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Six feet eight, hands the size of dinner plates, weeping. Percy will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Lead him gently” than after “Cuff him hard.” In New Inmate, waiting would only let someone else define what your silence meant.

choices.consequence: You commit to lead him gently. By Percy, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You choose to cuff him hard. It opens the route to Percy, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

You push through. The decision moves you toward Coffey's Hands and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Your hand on a lever, his eyes on yours, his last words a small request. “Throw it” opens the route to The Long Goodbye. “Stop the execution” changes the terms and carries you toward A Quiet Pension. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Coffey's Prayer in play.

choices.consequence: You commit to throw it. By The Long Goodbye, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.
You choose to stop the execution. It opens the route to A Quiet Pension, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. It opens the route to Coffey's Prayer, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Mr. Jingles is alive in a small wooden cage forty years later, and so are you, both of you tired of staying. The road into The Long Goodbye began with “Throw it” in Switch; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You leave the prison. You marry a kind woman. You wake up at night with green linoleum in your dreams. It does not let you go. The road into A Quiet Pension began with “Stop the execution” in Switch; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

On a hill behind the prison you bury a man with hands like dinner plates. You pray for a mercy you do not believe in, and it comes anyway. The road into Coffey's Prayer began with “Take the third path” in Switch; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
